reading.rtitle: Lunch on the Island: No Menu, Just Decisions
paras: On Saturday we had a plan: the ferry, the island, lunch by the water. But we didn't have a plan for the lunch. And that was the fun part.
At the Island Kitchen there wasn't a menu on the table. The waiter just said: “Today we have fresh fish, a fish soup and a chicken salad.” Leão didn't think for a second: “I'll have the fish.”
I couldn't decide. The waiter said the soup was a little spicy. “OK,” I said, “I'll try the soup.” Then Leão said: “And we'll share a salad.”
It was cold by the water, and I didn't have a jacket. Leão stood up: “Wait, I'll get my jacket from the bag. Here.”
At the end the waiter asked about dessert. “No, thank you, I won't have dessert,” I said. Then the bill came. “I'll pay this time,” I said. “OK,” he said, “but I'll leave the tip.”
Then it started to rain. “I'll call a taxi,” he said. But there are no taxis on the island! So we took the ferry back — wet, happy and full.

listenings.text: OK, I'm hungry. Let me see. The fish soup looks good, and it's cold today, so I'll have a bowl of soup. And bread? Yes, I'll take two pieces. My husband loves cheese, so I'll buy some cheese for him too. Wine? No, I won't buy wine today. We have a bottle at the hotel. Oh, look, fresh strawberries! They are cheap, so I'll take a box for the children. Oh no, it's raining. I don't have an umbrella. OK, I'll wait here ten minutes and I'll have a coffee.

Good evening, Mr. Silva. Front desk, how can I help? Your key doesn't work? I'm sorry. No problem, I'll send a new key to your room in five minutes. A taxi for tomorrow? Of course, I'll call one for six thirty. And breakfast? The restaurant opens at seven, but I'll ask the kitchen for a coffee at six. Don't worry, I won't forget. Anything else? An umbrella? Yes, I'll leave one at the door for you. Have a good night, Mr. Silva.
